subject: Uptime spectrum, response SLAs and discounting — CloudMetrics proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uptime spectrum, response SLAs and discounting — initial proposal

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion. Per our follow-up, attached is a concise SOW + an SLA sku matrix that maps our standard uptime bands (99.5 / 99.9 / 99.99) to response windows, on-call coverage, and associated retainer units. Quick summary: 

- 99.5%: Business-hours triage, 8-hour response, no retainer.
- 99.9%: 24/7 triage with 2-hour priority window + monthly on-call credit (1 retainer unit).
- 99.99%: Dedicated escalation lane, 30‑minute critical response, dedicated rotation (3 retainer units).

You mentioned a 12‑month commit and a desire to keep the effective unit price close to your current spend. Can you confirm the annual committed spend target and whether CloudMetrics prefers a single blended discount across tiers or tiered discounts by uptime band?

If helpful I can put together a short counterproposal showing blended vs tiered economics — I'll loop in pricing ops (Jonas) and our enterprise lead (Marissa) so we can move quickly.

Attachments: CloudMetrics_SOW_v1.pdf, redwood_uptime_sku_matrix.xlsx

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference for production
From: Elena Soto <elena@cloudmetrics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudmetrics.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime spectrum, response SLAs and discounting — initial proposal

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the matrix — helpful format. A few clarifications from our side before we commit to numbers: 

1) CloudMetrics is targeting ~ $1.2M annual spend for inference (hosted + dedicated burst lanes) with a 12‑month term.
2) We need a firm 99.9% uptime SLO for the primary region with documented runbook integration and quarterly SLA reports for audits.
3) Procurement will want an explicit discount ladder tied to commit bands (0-$500k, $500k-$1M, $1M+). Blended pricing is acceptable if the math is transparent.

Can you provide a counter with both a blended and a banded discount option and confirm whether the 99.9% lane can include a 2‑hour tech response and a single on-call credit per incident? Also, please confirm lead time for implementing the dedicated escalation lane (we have a planned peak in Q4).

Elena Soto
Head of Platform Operations, CloudMetrics
Elena.Soto@cloudmetrics.com
Attachment: procurement_requirements_v1.docx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: CloudMetrics — pricing approach options (internal)

Folks — forwarding Elena's ask. Notes / suggested approach:

- Deal target: $1.2M ARR / 12 months. Strategic reference customer for us on observability workloads.
- They require 99.9% SLO for primary region + quarterly compliance reports (SOC-like evidence).
- Procurement wants explicit commit bands.

Proposed concessions (tradeoffs we can sell):
1) Blended option: 18% discount off list across all tiers for $1.2M commit. Simpler to bill, easier for finance.
2) Banded option: 12% (0-$500k), 18% ($500k-$1M), 25% ($1M+) with a minimum 60‑day notice for SKU shift.
3) SLA uplift: 99.9% included; 99.99% requires a 3-retainer unit top-up and a 30% premium on compute-intensive tokens.
4) Implementation: dedicated escalation lane can be stood up in 6 weeks once SOC evidence and IP allowlist are completed.

Questions for legal / compliance: what language do we need for quarterly SLA reports (format + retention)? Also what hard commitments can we give on runbook integration timelines?

Please review and mark any redlines — I want to keep a narrow set of concessions we can offer without touching platform SLOs.

-Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudMetrics — pricing approach options (internal)

Thanks — quick operational notes.

- Finance prefers the banded discount (2) because it gives a clear incentive to push to $1M+. If we use blended (1) we should include a quarterly true-up clause so they don't get over-discounted while under-committing early.
- For SLA reporting: propose a standard CSV export with incidents + uptime % per region, retained 12 months, signed off by SRE lead. Legal can give final retention limits but compliance likes 12 months.
- On runbook integration: ask CloudMetrics to provide an runbook template; we can commit to building the mapping in 4 weeks post-PO for core playbooks, and 8 weeks for cross-team playbooks. Note: the dedicated escalation lane setup timeline is dependent on networking/KMS approvals (call out to ops).

I also suggest we keep a small credit bucket (one-time credit equal to 2% of first-year ARR) as a sign-of-goodwill if they sign within 14 days. Helps close.

-Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@cloudmetrics.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime spectrum, response SLAs and discounting — initial proposal

Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise counterproposal that includes both options (blended vs banded), an implementation timeline, and a draft SLA reporting template. High level: 

- Band-based discount (recommended): 12% / 18% / 25% with $1.2M ARR target and a 60‑day SKU stabilization window.
- SLA: 99.9% primary region SLO included; quarterly CSV reports retained 12 months. Runbook mapping: 4 weeks for core playbooks after PO.
- Implementation: dedicated escalation lane estimated 6 weeks post-network/KMS clearance.
- One-time sign-by credit: 2% of first-year ARR if executed within 14 days.

I've added the DocuSign link for the counteroffer and included the SOW + redlines as requested. If procurement wants to iterate, happy to get on a call tomorrow afternoon.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/3f1a9b
Attachments: 20270712-CM-counteroffer-redlines.docx, redwood_uptime_sku_matrix.xlsx

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
